authorities.review: Monitoring-plan content read. Internal trend trigger is newly authored and is not a legal limit. 2026 amendment crosscheck remains open.
Working-place examination timing, competent designation, adverse-condition response and record fields; no whole-mine compliance conclusion.
Contemporaneous agency description corroborates examination/record duties, not a new rule or substitute for actual examination evidence.

environmental_review.source_authorship_boundary: Existing September 5 synthetic retrospective calibration; no inference that laboratory evidence was available in August.

result.threshold_basis: New synthetic internal investigation trigger: latest minus 2019 annual mean > 0.005 mg/L. Not a statutory limit, background finding or permit exceedance.

environmental_review.interpretation: MW-17 latest uranium is 0.0232 mg/L against 2019 mean 0.01235 mg/L: +0.01085 mg/L. The internal trigger is exceeded. TAIL-UD-1 latest does not exceed that trigger, which does not establish absence of seepage or a hydraulic connection.

corrective_action.action: Joint groundwater/Cell 1 underdrain investigation: recover raw lab/QA and hydraulic evidence, evaluate license-specific action levels and reportability; preserve both source series. No final release pathway or liability determined.

reviewer_reperformance.method: Independent explicit arithmetic of four source baseline values and latest value; no professional audit opinion.
reviewer_reperformance.conclusion: Escalate; preserve unresolved pathway and liability.

documentary_reviews.result: FONSI is a decision supporting the plan scope; existing program describes mitigation but not completed mitigation checks. Do not relabel FONSI as annual permit renewal.

Existing qualified external-carrier boundary retained. ARU/BS&T ordinary acid-input service is not uranium carriage authority. Shipment-specific hazmat certification and carrier qualification remain required.
